title: Blinded data, non-tomographic
summary: The whole calibrated sample as one bin, measured blinded. The B-mode data vectors come first, in three estimators, each with its errors.
banner: Blinded (blind: unions): E-mode data vectors are concealed; do not interpret cosmology
provenance: ShapePipe v2.0.0 calibrated sample: 191.0M galaxies on all 22,901 run-1 tiles, 5,223 deg²
for the covariance only: the sum of the four bins of the recalibrated n(z) of CosmoStat/sp_validation#468
sp_validation run/alltiles-2d @ a4257516 (edge 28629e7b plus three fixes), measured 13 Nov

figures.caption: Blinded ξ± (black) split into pure E modes (blue), pure B modes (red) and ambiguous modes that cannot be assigned to either (grey), all multiplied by θ. Lensing makes no B modes, so they are a null test. Shading marks scales outside the fiducial 12′–83′; the vertical range is set by the points inside it.

figures.caption: B-mode COSEBIs Bₙ (complete orthogonal sets of E/B-integrals, a compact E/B split of ξ±) in units of their uncertainty, over the fiducial 12′–83′ (filled) and the full 1′–250′ (open). The headline null test uses n ≤ 6; higher modes are shaded.
figures.alt: B-mode COSEBIs Bₙ (complete orthogonal sets of E/B-integrals, a compact E/B split of ξ±) in units of their uncertainty, over the fiducial 12′–83′ (filled) and the full 1′–250′ (open). The headline null test uses n ≤ 6; higher modes are shaded.

figures.caption: Galaxy–PSF cross-correlations τ₂,₊ and τ₅,₊, multiplied by θ, for the catalogue without leakage correction. The band is the 68% range of the α, β, η leakage model of the raw catalogue over coefficient-resampling draws. Error bars are from the analytic τ covariance; points whose variance is not positive have none.

figures.caption: Galaxy–PSF cross-correlations τ₀, τ₂ and τ₅, fitted by the PSF leakage model with coefficients α (leakage), β (ellipticity residual) and η (size residual). The band is the model's 68% range over coefficient-resampling draws.
figures.alt: Galaxy–PSF cross-correlations τ₀, τ₂ and τ₅, fitted by the PSF leakage model with coefficients α (leakage), β (ellipticity residual) and η (size residual). The band is the model's 68% range over coefficient-resampling draws.

figures.caption: Coefficient-resampling draws of the leakage parameters (68 and 95% contours), not Bayesian samples. Axes omit 0.3% of each marginal tail. Full sample ranges: α [-0.00529, 0.0273]; β [1.05, 1.71]; η [-1.23, 2.72]. Displayed η range: [-0.677, 2.18].
figures.alt: Coefficient-resampling draws of the leakage parameters (68 and 95% contours), not Bayesian samples. Axes omit 0.3% of each marginal tail. Full sample ranges: α [-0.00529, 0.0273]; β [1.05, 1.71]; η [-1.23, 2.72]. Displayed η range: [-0.677, 2.18].

figures.caption: PSF leakage α₁, α₂ from weighted regressions of calibrated galaxy ellipticity on the PSF-model ellipticity at each galaxy, without object-wise leakage correction, in eight equal-count bins of resolution each split into eight equal-count bins of signal-to-noise. figures.caption: Change of the weighted mean calibrated ellipticity per standard deviation of each galaxy or PSF property (left), and that slope over its fit uncertainty (right; dotted at ±2). Slopes are fits to the means in 20 bins of each property, with shape-noise errors that omit spatially correlated noise, which matters most for RA and Dec. Galaxy size is √T; the size ratio is T/T_PSF.
figures.alt: Change of the weighted mean calibrated ellipticity per standard deviation of each galaxy or PSF property (left), and that slope over its fit uncertainty (right; dotted at ±2). figures.caption: Scale-dependent PSF leakage α(θ) = τ₀,₊/ρ₀,₊ for all galaxies and in tertiles of galaxy r magnitude, with jackknife errors. Each bin is calibrated with its own shear response plus the global selection response; the faint bin's selection response is larger, so its |α| is likely underestimated by about 10–20%.
figures.alt: Scale-dependent PSF leakage α(θ) = τ₀,₊/ρ₀,₊ for all galaxies and in tertiles of galaxy r magnitude, with jackknife errors. Each bin is calibrated with its own shear response plus the global selection response; the faint bin's selection response is larger, so its |α| is likely underestimated by about 10–20%.
